title: Unipotence is reflected by infinitesimal isogenies of smooth affine groups
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and fix an algebraic closure $\bar k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups below are affine $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. A torus is a group which becomes $\mathbf G_m^r$ over $\bar k$, for some integer $r\geq0$, where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. Unipotent means admitting, for some $n\geq1$, a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] into the upper unitriangular group $\mathcal U_{n,k}\subseteq\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group]: its $A$-points are upper triangular matrices with all diagonal entries $1$, for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$. Let $G,G'$ be smooth and connected, and let $f:G\to G'$ be a finite faithfully flat radicial homomorphism. Here finite means finite on coordinate rings, faithfully flat means flat and surjective, and radicial means injective on geometric points after every field extension. If $G'$ is unipotent, then $G$ is unipotent. No perfectness or characteristic assumption on $k$ is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 17.81, proof of the isogeny case, printed p.379 (the isogeny constructed in Proposition 17.80 is infinitesimal). Supporting geometric criterion: Corollaries 14.9 and 14.12, pp.282–283; functorial Jordan decomposition, Theorem 9.18 and paragraph 9.19, pp.170–171; unitriangular form, Theorem 14.5, pp.281–282.

proof.text: Put $K=\bar k$. Choose $m\geq1$ and a closed faithful representation $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}_{m,k}$ by [lem-sfb-affine-group-faithful-linear-representation]. By the assumed unipotence of $G'$, choose its defining closed immersion $j:G'\hookrightarrow\mathcal U_{n,k}\subseteq\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}$, with $n\geq1$. Form $G_K$ and $G'_K$. The affine fibre-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies their coordinate rings with $K\otimes_k k[G]$ and $K\otimes_k k[G']$. They are finitely generated $K$-algebras: tensor a finite set of algebra generators with $1$. The tensor universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] identifies $G_K(R)$ with $G(R)$ for every commutative $K$-algebra $R$ viewed as a $k$-algebra, compatibly with the group operations. In particular $\rho_K$ and $j_K$ remain injective on every such set of points. Write $F=f_K$. The radicial hypothesis gives injectivity of $F:G_K(K)\to G'_K(K)$ directly, since $K$ is algebraically closed.

source.place: Theorem 4.9 and Corollary 4.10, p.87; Proposition 17.81, p.379, infinitesimal isogeny case; scalar-extension conventions.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary $g\in G_K(K)$. For every finite-dimensional rational representation $(V,r_V)$ of $G_K$, set $\lambda_V=(r_V(g))_u$, the unipotent matrix factor supplied by [lem-sfb-multiplicative-jordan-linear-compatibility]. These factors are invertible. If $a:V\to W$ is equivariant, then $a r_V(g)=r_W(g)a$, so the intertwiner clause gives $a\lambda_V=\lambda_W a$. The tensor clause gives $\lambda_{V\otimes W}=\lambda_V\otimes\lambda_W$. On the unit representation $r_{\mathbf1}(g)=I$; its decomposition $I=I\cdot I$ and uniqueness give $\lambda_{\mathbf1}=I$. The zero representation is covered by the same cited matrix theorem. These are precisely the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-tannaka-rational-point-reconstruction], so it supplies $h\in G_K(K)$ such that $r_V(h)=(r_V(g))_u$ for every finite-dimensional rational representation. This constructs the unipotent part inside the group; it does not assume that matrix decomposition stays in an arbitrary closed subgroup.

source.place: Theorem 9.18 proof, p.170, applying Theorem 9.2 to the family of unipotent parts; Propositions 9.13 and 9.15, p.169.

proof.text: Apply the preceding identity to the representation $r=j_K\circ F$ of $G_K$ on $K^n$. Since $j$ factors through $\mathcal U_n$, the matrix $A=r(g)$ is upper unitriangular. Its difference $A-I_n$ is strictly upper triangular, and $(A-I_n)^n=0$: an entry of a product of $n$ such matrices is a sum indexed by strictly increasing chains of $n+1$ indices in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, of which there are none. Hence $A=I_n\cdot A=A\cdot I_n$ is a decomposition of the required kind. Uniqueness in [lem-sfb-multiplicative-jordan-linear-compatibility] gives $A_u=A$. Step 2 therefore says $j_K(F(h))=r(h)=A_u=A=j_K(F(g))$. Injectivity of $j_K$ on $K$-points gives $F(h)=F(g)$, and radicial injectivity from Step 1 gives $h=g$. No inference from geometric injectivity to a closed immersion is used.

source.place: Theorem 9.18 and paragraphs 9.19--9.21, pp.170--171; Proposition 17.81, p.379, infinitesimal isogeny case; unitriangular matrices as in Theorem 14.5.

proof.text: Now take $r_V=\rho_K$ in Step 2. Since $h=g$, it gives $\rho_K(g)=(\rho_K(g))_u$. By the unipotent-factor clause of [lem-sfb-multiplicative-jordan-linear-compatibility], $(\rho_K(g)-I_m)^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$. The point $g\in G(K)$ was arbitrary. Thus the faithful representation $\rho$ chosen over $k$ sends every geometric point of $G$ to a unipotent matrix. Apply [lem-sfb-geometric-unipotence-unitriangular-embedding] to $G$ and $\rho$: $G$ is smooth, affine and of finite type by hypothesis, $m\geq1$, and $\rho$ is injective on every algebra-valued point by Step 1. The cited statement supplies a closed immersion over $k$ into $\mathcal U_{d,k}$ for some $d\geq1$, exactly the required unipotence. Its conclusion is over $k$ itself, so no descent of a chosen geometric flag is assumed.

source.place: Corollary 14.12, p.283, with Theorem 14.5, pp.281--282; Theorem 9.18 and paragraph 9.19, pp.170--171.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 17.81, p.379, infinitesimal isogeny case, expanded using the reconstruction proof of Theorem 9.18, p.170, and Corollary 14.12 with Theorem 14.5, pp.281--283.

Step 1: the faithful-representation node gives ρ injective on all A-points; the tensor universal property gives G_K(R)=G(R); radicial gives injectivity of F on K-points. Step 4: ρ(g) is unipotent for every geometric point g, and every hypothesis of the geometric-unipotence-unitriangular-embedding node holds; it concludes a closed immersion into U_n over k.
